english.note: Use this as the default verb when someone hints at something without saying it directly.
This is the all-purpose choice for referring indirectly or hinting at something without saying it outright.
Choose 暗示 when the meaning is hinted at indirectly rather than stated openly or entailed logically.
Use 暗示 when implying something without stating it openly.

examples.english: They never said directly that they disliked it, but their sour face all evening seemed to imply that they were unhappy with the arrangement.
examples.traditional: 佢冇直接話唔鍾意，但成晚黑面，暗示佢對個安排好不滿。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 mou5 zik6 zip3 waa6 m4 zung1 ji3 daan6 seng4 maan5 hak1 min6 am3 si6 keoi5 deoi3 go3 on1 paai4 hou2 bat1 mun5

examples.english: They allude to not wanting to take part by staying quiet all evening.
examples.traditional: 佢成晚都唔出聲，其實係暗示唔想參加。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 maan5 dou1 m4 ceot1 seng1 kei4 sat6 hai6 am3 si6 m4 soeng2 caam1 gaa1

examples.english: Their sudden question about whether I was free can connote that they want to ask me to dinner.
examples.traditional: 佢突然問我得唔得閒，暗示住想約我食飯。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 dat6 jin4 man6 ngo5 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4 am3 si6 zyu6 soeng2 joek3 ngo5 sik6 faan6

examples.english: That way of putting it can suggest that he does not want to help.
examples.traditional: 佢咁樣講，暗示緊佢唔想幫手。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 gam2 joeng2 gong2 am3 si6 gan2 keoi5 m4 soeng2 bong1 sau2
